 Uttar Pradesh DGME opens 115 MBBS and BDS seats in stray vacancy round. Merit list released; choice filling ends November 12. Check eligibility and deadlines.
 MedAdmit News Desk · 10 Nov 2026 · 4 min read The Directorate General of Medical Education and Training (DGME) in Uttar Pradesh has announced a stray vacancy round for NEET UG 2026, releasing 115 unfilled seats across government and private medical and dental colleges in the state. This is your final opportunity to secure an MBBS or BDS seat if you were not allotted a college in earlier counselling rounds. The merit list has been published, and eligible candidates must act quickly—choice filling closes on November 12, 2026. Understanding the seat distribution, eligibility rules, and tight timeline is critical to making the most of this round.
 If your name appears on the UP NEET 2026 stray vacancy merit list and you have completed registration and document verification, you must fill your college choices by November 12, 2026, 11 AM to participate in this final round of seat allotment.

 Unlock My College List What is the stray vacancy round and why does it matter?
 A stray vacancy round is the final counselling phase after all earlier rounds of seat allotment. It exists to fill seats that remain empty—either because candidates rejected their allotment, did not report to college, or withdrew from the process. For NEET aspirants who did not secure a seat in the main or subsequent counselling rounds, this is often the last chance to gain admission to an MBBS or BDS programme in Uttar Pradesh.
 The stray vacancy round typically has fewer seats and lower cutoff scores than earlier rounds, making it accessible to candidates with lower NEET ranks. However, the competition is still real, and seats fill quickly based on merit rank and choice order. Missing the choice-filling deadline means automatic exclusion from this round.
 How many seats are available and where are they located?
 A total of 115 seats have been released: 93 MBBS seats and 22 BDS seats. The critical distinction is that only 11 of these seats are in government institutions, while 104 are in private colleges. This means the vast majority of vacancies are in the private sector, which typically charges higher fees than government colleges.
 Government seats: 11 total (10 MBBS + 1 BDS) 
 Private seats: 104 total (83 MBBS + 21 BDS) 
 Government MBBS vacancies are spread across Autonomous State Medical Colleges in Sonbhadra, Bahraich, Hardoi, Jaunpur, and Sultanpur, plus other government medical colleges 
 Who is eligible to participate in the stray vacancy round?
 Only candidates whose names appear on the official merit list published by DGME can participate. However, being on the merit list is not enough. You must also have completed all of the following before the choice-filling deadline:
 Know the exact MBBS/BDS colleges your rank can get
 Official 2023–2025 closing ranks and fees, matched to your rank.
 See My Colleges Completed your registration on the official UP NEET counselling portal (upneet.gov.in), paid the required security deposit fee, and had your documents verified by the counselling authority. If any of these steps are incomplete, you will not be able to fill choices or receive an allotment, even if your name is on the merit list. The merit list contains 2,546 registered candidates, but not all may be eligible if they have not finished the verification process.
 Your name must appear on the published merit list 
 You must have completed registration on upneet.gov.in 
 You must have paid the security fee 
 Your documents must have been verified 
 What are the key dates and deadlines?
 The stray vacancy round operates on a compressed timeline. The merit list was released on November 7, 2026, and choice filling began the same day. However, the critical deadline is November 12, 2026, at 11 AM—this is when choice filling closes. After this time, no further choices can be submitted, and you will be excluded from the round.
 Merit list release: November 7, 2026 
 Choice filling begins: November 7, 2026 
 Choice filling deadline: November 12, 2026, 11 AM (HARD DEADLINE) 
 Seat allotment result: November 12, 2026 
 Admission reporting period: November 13–16, 2026 
 How does the choice-filling and allotment process work?
 After you verify your eligibility and log into the portal, you will be asked to rank the colleges and courses you wish to be considered for, in order of preference. The allotment algorithm then matches your rank and choices to available seats. Seats are allotted based on your merit rank and the order in which you ranked your choices—higher-ranked candidates get priority, and within each rank, the system respects your preference order.
 On November 12, 2026, the allotment result will be released. If you are allotted a seat, you will receive an allotment letter and must report to your assigned college between November 13 and November 16, 2026, to complete admission formalities such as document submission, fee payment, and hostel registration. Failure to report within this window may result in forfeiture of your seat.
 What should you do right now if you are eligible?
 First, check the merit list immediately on upneet.gov.in or via the direct PDF link provided by DGME. Search for your name and confirm your rank. If you are on the list and have completed registration and document verification, log into the portal and begin filling your choices without delay. Do not wait until the last moment—portal congestion on the final day can cause technical issues.

Remember that government seats are rare in this round, so if you are eligible for a government college, prioritize it in your choices. Private colleges vary widely in quality and cost; choose wisely based on your financial capacity and career goals. Once you submit your choices, you cannot change them, so think through your ranking before finalizing.
 What happens if you are allotted a seat?
 If your name appears in the allotment result on November 12, you will be assigned to a specific college and course based on your rank and choices. You will receive an allotment letter (usually downloadable from the portal) that specifies your college, course, and reporting date. You must then visit your assigned college in person between November 13 and November 16, 2026, to complete admission formalities.
 At the college, you will be required to submit original documents (10th and 12th certificates, NEET admit card, NEET result, Aadhaar, caste certificate if applicable, and other documents as per the college's checklist), pay the first semester or annual fee, and register for hostel accommodation if needed. Bring all documents in original and photocopied form. Failure to report or complete formalities within the deadline will result in cancellation of your allotment and loss of the seat.
 What if you are not on the merit list or do not get allotted?
 If your name does not appear on the merit list, you are not eligible for this round. This typically means your NEET rank is below the cutoff for the stray vacancy round, or you did not complete registration and verification in time. In this case, you may consider private medical colleges that conduct their own entrance exams or admission processes, or you may prepare for NEET 2027 if you wish to attempt the exam again.
 If you are on the merit list but do not receive an allotment in this round, it means all your preferred colleges were filled by higher-ranked candidates before your turn, or you ranked colleges in a way that did not match available seats. You can then explore direct admission routes at private colleges or consider other medical education pathways.
 Key takeaways for NEET aspirants in Uttar Pradesh
 The stray vacancy round is a genuine opportunity, but it requires speed and precision. With only 115 seats and a merit list of 2,546 candidates, competition is real. The tight timeline—just five days for choice filling—means you cannot afford to be complacent. Check the merit list today, verify your eligibility, and fill your choices well before the November 12 deadline.
 Remember that most seats (104 out of 115) are in private colleges, which charge significantly higher fees than government institutions. Factor in the total cost of education before ranking private colleges. Finally, once you submit your choices, they are final—there is no revision. Think carefully about your college preferences and rank them in an order that reflects both your aspirations and your realistic chances based on your rank.

 How do I check if my name is on the UP NEET 2026 stray vacancy merit list?
 Visit the official UP NEET counselling portal at upneet.gov.in and log in with your credentials. Search for your name in the merit list, or download the merit list PDF directly from the portal. You can also search by your NEET roll number or registration number. If your name appears, note your rank, as this will determine your priority in seat allotment.
 What is the difference between government and private seats in this round?
 Government seats (11 total) are in state-run medical colleges and typically charge lower fees, around ₹50,000–₹1,50,000 per year. Private seats (104 total) are in private medical colleges and charge significantly higher fees, often ₹10–₹20 lakhs per year or more. Government seats are highly competitive; private seats offer more availability but at a much higher cost. Choose based on your financial capacity and career goals.
 What happens if I miss the November 12 choice-filling deadline?
 If you do not fill your choices by November 12, 2026, at 11 AM, you will be automatically excluded from the stray vacancy round. There is no extension or grace period. You will not be eligible for any seat allotment in this round. Plan ahead and submit your choices well before the deadline to avoid technical issues or last-minute delays.
 Can I change my college choices after I submit them?
 No. Once you submit your choices on the portal, they are final and cannot be revised. The allotment algorithm will process your choices in the order you ranked them. Therefore, think carefully about your preferences before submitting. Rank colleges in an order that reflects your genuine preference and realistic chances based on your NEET rank.
 What documents do I need to bring when I report to my allotted college?
 Bring original and photocopied versions of: NEET admit card, NEET result scorecard, 10th and 12th mark sheets and certificates, Aadhaar card, caste certificate (if applicable), domicile certificate, medical fitness certificate, and any other documents specified by your college. Check your college's admission checklist on their website or allotment letter to confirm the exact list. Incomplete documentation may delay or cancel your admission.
 If I am allotted a seat, how long do I have to report to the college?
 You must report to your allotted college between November 13 and November 16, 2026, to complete admission formalities. This is a hard deadline. If you do not report within this window, your seat will be cancelled and offered to the next candidate on the merit list. Plan your travel and document submission in advance to meet this deadline.
 What is the security fee, and do I need to pay it again for the stray vacancy round?
 The security fee is a refundable deposit (typically ₹50,000–₹1,00,000) paid during initial registration to confirm your participation in counselling. If you have already paid this fee during an earlier counselling round and your registration is active, you do not need to pay it again for the stray vacancy round. However, if your registration has expired or you are registering for the first time, you must pay the fee before filling choices.
 Are there any seats reserved for SC, ST, or OBC candidates in the stray vacancy round?
 Yes. The seat matrix includes reservations as per government norms. The exact number of reserved seats for each category is specified in the official seat matrix PDF released by DGME. Check the seat matrix on upneet.gov.in to see how many seats are reserved for your category at each college. Your eligibility for reserved seats depends on your caste certificate and the college's reservation policy.
 If your name is on the merit list, act immediately: verify your eligibility, log into upneet.gov.in, and fill your college choices by November 12, 2026, at 11 AM. Once allotted, report to your college between November 13 and 16 with all required documents. This is your final opportunity to secure an MBBS or BDS seat in Uttar Pradesh for 2026—do not let it slip away.
